in the village, pools of light moved with the guards torches, and the view was a wide variety of all forest and land the area could raise. she almost missed it then, searching out a valley to the right of steel hill. she might have looked anyways, but only she seemed to be awake and out at this hour, and reacting to this strange event. it zapped into the sky, like lightning. and suddenly it fell, spilling coarse fire like smoke.

almost the whole village was lit with faint red, and as quickly as it had arrived, it slipped below the treeline. she could have sworn though, that the, thing, moved in its flight. the guards began shouting outside, and the spilling red trail was disappearing at its leisure. the village had always said that she had an imagination for the world. she thought they were ignorant, and that it was an intuition. the falling red thing was tickling that intuition.

while it was still fresh, she hurriedly grabbed parchment and sticks of charcoal she had secreted away, and sketched out a map as exact as she could. she kept up her vigil, now looking at her door with anxiety. later, she was going to have some exploring to do.
